# A Complete Guide to Virtual Memory, Allocators, Paging, and Performance in the Modern Linux Kernel {.unnumbered}

Memory management is the most intricate, performance-critical, and ubiquitous subsystem within the Linux kernel. Every memory read, instruction fetch, process spawn, buffer allocation, network packet transfer, and disk write directly interacts with the virtual memory (VM) and physical memory management layers.

Operating at the tight intersection between CPU hardware microarchitecture (MMUs, TLBs, cache hierarchies) and abstract user-space runtimes, the Linux memory subsystem balances competing engineering priorities: strict process isolation, near-zero translation latency, deterministic physical page allocation, fragmentation avoidance, and resilient reclaim under severe memory pressure.

This section provides an exhaustive, kernel-level curriculum covering modern Linux memory management from first principles to kernel source code walkthroughs, low-level data structures, hardware address translation, kernel allocators, user-space memory engines, page cache mechanics, NUMA placement, cgroups v2 resource limits, OOM resilience, and performance optimization.

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   LINUX MEMORY MANAGEMENT TAXONOMY                     │
│                                                                        │
│   User-Space Runtimes & Applications                                   │
│   ├─ glibc ptmalloc3 (Arenas/Bins), jemalloc, tcmalloc                 │
│   └─ Process VMA Tree: text, data, BSS, heap (brk), mmap, stack        │
│                                │                                       │
│                                ▼                                       │
│   Kernel Virtual Memory Subsystem (mm/)                                │
│   ├─ Virtual Address Translation: 4-Level/5-Level Paging (PGD->P4D->   │
│   │  PUD->PMD->PTE), Transparent Huge Pages (2 MiB / 1 GiB), TLB      │
│   ├─ Demand Paging & Faults: do_page_fault(), Copy-on-Write (COW)      │
│   ├─ Dynamic Kernel Allocations: vmalloc, vmap, ioremap                │
│   └─ Page Cache & VFS: Folios, XArrays, Readahead, Dirty Writeback     │
│                                │                                       │
│                                ▼                                       │
│   Object & Slab Allocator Layer                                        │
│   ├─ SLUB Allocator: Per-CPU kmem_cache_cpu (lockless), kmalloc()      │
│   └─ Historical Allocators: SLAB (queues), SLOB (embedded list)        │
│                                │                                       │
│                                ▼                                       │
│   Physical Page Allocator (Buddy Allocator)                            │
│   ├─ Free Lists (Orders 0 to 10: 4 KiB to 4 MiB chunks)                │
│   ├─ Memory Zones: ZONE_DMA, ZONE_DMA32, ZONE_NORMAL, ZONE_MOVABLE    │
│   └─ Memory Nodes: NUMA pg_data_t, Zoned Allocator, Watermarks (wmark) │
│                                │                                       │
│                                ▼                                       │
│   Hardware Architecture (x86-64, ARM64, RISC-V)                        │
│   └─ MMU, Page Table Walkers, TLB Shootdowns, Caches (L1/L2/L3), DRAM │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
